learning: Speed (base_speed 1.6 to 1.4) did not clear losses in iteration 9, so the loss is sensing-driven at forward rows. This race tests the intermediate row at the wider span. The oval floor near 0.061 is not expected to move.
notes: Builder's y=0.05, ±0.06 geometry with the iteration 9 controller unchanged, so the geometry is the only variable. Expected: line losses on s-bend and slalom fall toward 0 if the forward row and wider span both matter.
rationale: The Builder's iteration-10 geometry moves the forward row to y=0.05 and widens the outer sensors to x=±0.06, keeping 16 mm footprints, 0.12 m track, 0.035 m wheels, 0.6 kg mass and the 0.16 x 0.12 m body. Iteration 9 (y=0.045, ±0.055, base_speed 1.6 to 1.4) still logged 0.9 line losses on s-bend and 1.0 on slalom, so curve speed did not cause the losses. Iterations 6 to 8 showed the forward row is the source: y=0.03 gave zero losses, while y=0.045 to 0.06 gave roughly one per trial. The off-track floor (max_error about 0.061) has not moved under any geometry or gain change, so it is not treated as a lever. Because speed is ruled out, I keep the iteration 9 controller exactly (base_speed 1.4, kp 2.5, ki 0.5, kd 0.15, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction). That isolates the geometry change. The only controller-side question is whether losses remain at the intermediate row; if they do, the next step is geometric, not a gain change. Expected: line losses may fall if ±0.06 at y=0.05 covers the curve edge. I do not state a result.
